source: Numista N#6133 (https://en.numista.com/catalogue/pieces6133.html): Austria 20 heller 1916-1918, KM#2826, Charles I, iron, 3.5 g, 21 mm, engraver Stefan Schwartz, obverse crowned double-headed eagle with the Austrian shield, reverse value in a wreath with the date below and no legend; 1918 mintage 48,985,000 (also https://numisquare.com/20-heller-1916-1918-1077918220.html). The C023 photo (photos/p1/C023_rev.webp) is that reverse exactly: large 20 in an oak wreath, 1918 below, toothed border, no lettering; no German Empire 20 pfennig was struck in 1918. Found by Gemini (HW-gemini-story-check-20261021-1), checked by Claude.

old: A 1918 20 Heller from the Austrian Empire (previously cataloged as a German 20 Pfennig). Large 20 in oak wreath with date 1918 below on the reverse, crowned double-headed Austrian eagle on the obverse (Stefan Schwartz). Struck in iron during WWI.
new: A 1918 20-heller coin from Austria, struck in iron during the First World War under Emperor Charles I, when copper and nickel went to the war. The side shown has a large 20 in an oak wreath with the date 1918 below and no lettering; the other side shows the crowned double-headed eagle with the Austrian shield. Stefan Schwartz engraved it.

old: Type record describes an imperial German Empire iron 20 pfennig dated 1918, but reference checks (Greysheet, NGC) list no imperial iron 20 pfennig: the imperial 20pf ended in 1877 (KM#5) and the WWI iron issues were 5pf (KM#19) and 10pf (KM#20) only. Iron 20pf pieces dated 1918 exist as municipal notgeld. Is this coin a city notgeld piece misfiled under the imperial issuer? Verify against the physical coin or photo.

Owner believes this is German. Photo side: 20 in an oak wreath, 1918, toothed border, iron, which fits a German city notgeld (emergency) 20 pfennig (the Empire struck no 1918 20 pfennig). Read the city name on the other side and re-file the type. Confirm at Phase 2 (pro photos); the owner's pen label may be wrong.
